transcript.text: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas

This is a very common issue with Bosch condenser dryers (like the WTN85201GB). Since it’s a condenser model, it doesn’t vent outside; instead, it cools moist air to turn water into liquid, which collects in a tank or drains away. If clothes are still damp after 2 hours, the heat isn’t being applied efficiently, or moisture isn’t being removed properly.

Here’s a step-by-step troubleshooting guide, ordered from most likely/easiest to more complex:

### 1. Clean the Condenser Unit (Most Common Cause)
The condenser is a plastic unit with fins located at the bottom front of the dryer (usually behind a flap or grille). If it’s clogged with lint, airflow and heat exchange are severely reduced.
• How to fix:
• Pull out the condenser unit.
• Rinse it under warm water from top to bottom until the water runs clear. Use a soft brush if needed (no harsh chemicals).
• Let it dry completely before reinserting.
• Check monthly.

### 2. Clean the Lint Filter(s)
There are usually two filters: one in the door rim and one near the condenser.
• How to fix: Remove both, wash them under warm water, and ensure they’re completely dry before putting them back. A clogged filter restricts airflow.

### 3. Check the Water Pump & Drain Hose (If you use drain hose)
If your dryer is connected to a waste pipe instead of using the water tank:
• The pump can fail or get blocked by lint/fluff.
• Check: Ensure the drain hose isn’t kinked, bent, or clogged. Listen for the pump running during the cycle (a humming sound). If it’s silent, the pump may be dead.

### 4. Empty the Water Tank
If you’re using the tank:
• Make sure it’s completely empty before starting.
• Check that the float mechanism inside the tank isn’t stuck (it should move freely up and down).

### 5. Clean the Heat Exchanger / Condenser Housing
Over time, lint can build up in the housing around the condenser unit or on the fan blades behind it.
• How to fix: Use a vacuum cleaner with a brush attachment to clean out lint from the cavity where the condenser sits and around the fan area.

### 6. Check for Overloading or Underloading
• Overloading: Too many clothes prevent proper airflow and tumbling. Reduce load size by ~20%.
• Underloading: Very small loads (e.g., one towel) can cause sensors to misread dryness. Add a couple of similar items if the load is tiny.

### 7. Sensor Cleaning (Moisture Sensors)
Some Bosch models have moisture sensors inside the drum (usually two metal strips). If they’re coated with fabric softener residue, they can’t detect dampness accurately and shut off early.
• How to fix: Wipe the sensor strips with a cloth dipped in white vinegar or rubbing alcohol.

### 8. Check the Thermostat or Heating Element
If the condenser is clean and airflow is good, but the air inside isn’t hot:
• The heating element may be failing.
• The thermal fuse (safety device) may have blown due to overheating.
• Test: Run a cycle with no clothes. If the air coming out after 10–15 minutes is not warm/hot, the heating system has failed. This requires professional repair or part replacement.

### 9. Error Codes
Check the display for any error codes (e.g., E15, E24, etc.). Refer to your user manual:
• E15/E24: Often related to water drainage issues.
• Other codes: May indicate sensor or electronic faults.

---

### Quick Diagnostic Test:
1. Clean the condenser and lint filters thoroughly.
2. Run a Cottons 60°C cycle with no clothes for 30 minutes.
3. After 15–20 minutes, carefully feel the air coming out of the door seal or vent area (don’t touch hot surfaces).
• If it’s cold: Heating element or thermostat failure → Call a technician.
• If it’s warm/hot but clothes are still damp in normal loads: Likely airflow restriction (condenser/fan) or sensor issue.

### When to Call a Professional:
• If the condenser is clean and filters are clear, but no heat is produced.
• If you hear unusual grinding noises (fan motor issue).
• If error codes persist after cleaning.
• If you’re not comfortable opening the back panel to check internal components.

Start with cleaning the condenser—this solves 80% of "not drying properly" issues in Bosch condenser dryers. Let me know if you find any specific symptoms during your checks!

Did the cleaning. The condenser had never been cleaned and the front was matted with lint, but it rinsed clean with the shower head. The door filters had fluff and a waxy film and needed scrubbing. I vacuumed fluff from the slot behind the condenser and wiped the dull sensor bars with vinegar. It's hot inside the drum after 20 mins. No error codes, just the 'clean filter' symbol sometimes. Should I do a test cycle now?

Yes, you should absolutely run a test cycle now. You have addressed the most common causes of poor drying performance: restricted airflow (lint blockage), dirty heat exchange surfaces, and sensor interference.

However, before you start, please note one important detail about your model: The WTN85201GB is a Heat Pump dryer, not a standard condenser. This changes the troubleshooting slightly because it uses a refrigerant cycle to extract moisture more efficiently than older condenser models. The "clean filter" symbol appearing intermittently can sometimes indicate that the system detects reduced airflow or sensor issues, even if the filters look clean.

### Recommended Test Cycle:
1.  Load: Use a medium load (e.g., 5–6 towels). Don’t overload it.
2.  Program: Select "Cottons" at 40°C (lower temp is better for testing efficiency) or the "AutoDry" / "Sensor Dry" program if available. Avoid "Time Dry" programs as they don’t rely on sensors.
3.  Check Settings: Ensure no extra options like "Extra Dry" or "Iron Dry" are selected, as these can extend drying time unnecessarily.
4.  Monitor: Listen for the compressor and fan running smoothly. The drum should feel warm/hot after 20–30 minutes.

### What to Watch For:
• Drying Time: A properly functioning heat pump dryer should dry a medium cotton load in 1.5–2.5 hours, depending on humidity. If it’s still damp after 2 hours, the issue may be deeper than airflow.
• Error Codes: Keep an eye out for any new codes (e.g., F05, F18, etc.).

### If It Still Doesn’t Dry Properly:
Since you’ve cleaned everything, here are the next most likely causes for a Bosch Heat Pump dryer:

1.  Thermistor/NTC Sensor Failure: Even though you wiped the sensor bars, the internal thermistors (which measure air temperature) can fail or drift out of calibration. This is common in older units.
2.  Refrigerant Leak: If the compressor runs but doesn’t get cold enough to condense moisture effectively, there may be a leak in the sealed refrigerant system. This requires a professional technician.
3.  Fan Motor Issue: The internal fan (which circulates air through the heat exchanger) might be running slower than it should due to wear or bearing issues, reducing efficiency.
4.  Control Board Glitch: Sometimes the main PCB can have intermittent faults. A power reset (unplug for 10 minutes) can sometimes clear this.

### Quick Reset Before You Start:
• Unplug the dryer from the mains for 10–15 minutes. This resets the control board and clears any temporary glitches.
• Plug it back in and start your test cycle.

Let me know how the test cycle goes! If it still fails, we can look into specific error codes or component testing.
Ran the test cycle. Clothes dried in about 100 minutes and the water container was nearly full, so it looks sorted. Is there anything I should do to stop it happening again?

That’s great news! 100 minutes is a very reasonable time for a heat pump dryer, especially if you were using a lower temperature setting like 40°C. Since the water container was nearly full, we know the machine is successfully extracting moisture from your clothes.

To prevent this from happening again and to keep your Bosch WTN85201GB running efficiently, here’s a maintenance schedule:

### The "Every Load" Routine
• Clean the Door Filters: This is non-negotiable. Even if they look okay, give them a quick rinse under warm water every 3–4 loads. The waxy film you mentioned can build up quickly from fabric softeners or dryer sheets (if you use them).
• Empty the Water Tank: Don’t wait for it to overflow. A full tank can sometimes trigger sensors incorrectly or just be inconvenient.

### The "Monthly" Routine
• Deep Clean the Condenser: Since yours was heavily matted with lint, you might want to check it every 4–6 weeks. Rinse it under warm water and let it dry completely before sliding it back in. A wet condenser can reduce efficiency and cause odors.
• Vacuum the Housing: While the condenser is out, give the cavity behind it a quick vacuum with a brush attachment to remove any loose fluff that might have settled there.

### Tips for Better Drying & Longevity
• Avoid Fabric Softeners on Towels/Active Wear: These can leave a residue that blocks the pores of fabrics and coats the condenser fins, reducing heat exchange efficiency over time.
• Check Pockets: Coins or keys can damage the drum or block airflow sensors.
• Don’t Overload: Heat pump dryers need space for air to circulate. If you stuff it full, clothes will take much longer to dry and may come out damp.
• Use a Lint Brush: Keep a small brush handy to wipe down the rubber door seal occasionally; lint can accumulate there and fall into the machine later.

### When to Call a Professional
If you notice the drying time creeping back up (e.g., taking 3+ hours for cottons) despite regular cleaning, it might be time for a service technician to check:
• The thermistors (temperature sensors).
• The heat pump compressor and refrigerant levels.

For now, stick to your new routine, and you should enjoy many more years of efficient drying!
